artifacts.caption: Raw DevTools performance trace for independent inspection

findings.evidence: The dark/reduced-motion screenshot is visually identical to the light capture: white surfaces and light content cards remain; no usable dark theme is applied.
findings.suggestedFix: Add color-scheme: light dark and theme surfaces/text with prefers-color-scheme or light-dark().

findings.summary: Navigation and carousel state changes do not use declarative modern motion
findings.evidence: UI probe found no page animation and no authored container CSS; DOM/CSS inspection found no View Transition or scroll-timeline usage despite carousel and route/state navigation.
findings.suggestedFix: Progressively enhance route/state changes with View Transitions and use CSS scroll timelines for any scroll-linked effects, with reduced-motion handling.

findings.summary: Navigation provides little state or attention guidance
findings.evidence: Screenshots and DOM show static desktop navigation/chrome; route changes and in-page navigation provide no directional transition, progress cue, or scroll-aware adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Add current-location cues and progressive directional transitions; make sticky chrome respond to scroll state without JS scroll handlers.

findings.summary: Consent wall interrupts every primary path
findings.evidence: First-load screenshots on homepage, article, search, and 410 show a large custom role=dialog consent wall obscuring the primary content; article capture additionally shows a blank white modal state.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a compact, semantic dialog that never enters blank state, preserves immediate reject/manage access, and avoids obscuring the whole article more than necessary.

findings.summary: Dense chrome and advertising compete with news content
findings.evidence: Homepage and section screenshots devote substantial space to nav bars, side rails, ad placeholders, topic chips, and repeated modules, competing with headlines and article content.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce duplicate nav bands and side modules, collapse low-priority ad/topic chrome, and prioritize headline/content hierarchy.

findings.summary: Mobile layout is a clipped 1200 px desktop canvas
findings.evidence: At a 360x800 viewport, layout reported scrollWidth 1200, clientWidth 360, and 840 px horizontal overflow; the screenshot shows only a clipped desktop slice.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the forced 1200 px layout/viewport behavior; use intrinsic grids, minmax(), fluid sizing, and narrow-layout tests with zero horizontal overflow.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is invisible and some touch targets collide
findings.evidence: Programmatic focus on the first visible link produced outline: none 0px. Lighthouse also reported target-size failures for tightly spaced links/buttons.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide a high-contrast :focus-visible ring and increase target size/spacing to at least the accessibility guidance minimum.

findings.summary: Mobile loading and visual stability miss Core Web Vitals targets
findings.evidence: Mobile Lighthouse measured LCP 4.5 s, FCP 3.4 s, CLS 0.295, Speed Index 5.9 s, and performance score 0.58; the trace corroborated load activity through 11.26 s.
findings.suggestedFix: Prioritize the LCP content, reserve all dynamic/advertising space, and delay non-critical work until after content and interaction readiness.

findings.summary: Heavy script and stylesheet delivery wastes the critical path
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 205 requests and 5,018,815 transferred bytes, including 52 scripts/2.86 MB and multiple parser-inserted very-high-priority stylesheets; Lighthouse estimated 303 KiB unused JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Deduplicate analytics, conditionally load advertising/video code, split route-specific code, and consolidate/defer non-critical styles.

findings.evidence: Search probe found an input with no associated label and a submit button with no accessible label text; the page title is also the generic homepage title.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a persistent or visually-hidden label for the search input and an aria-label or visible name for its submit button.

findings.summary: Third-party failures surface as browser errors and inspector issues
findings.evidence: Lighthouse reported a browser console error (third-party beacon HTTP 422) and a DevTools cookie inspector issue.
findings.suggestedFix: Handle or remove the failing beacon and resolve third-party cookie inspector warnings so production loads cleanly.

findings.evidence: Image audit found 18 oversized images, 47 without srcset, 3 below-fold images not lazy-loaded, 2 legacy-format images, and 1 missing alt.
findings.suggestedFix: Add srcset/sizes, serve thumbnails near rendered dimensions, lazy-load below-fold media, retain dimensions, and fix the missing alt.

findings.summary: Browser security policy and cookie flags are incomplete
findings.evidence: Headers audit found no Content-Security-Policy or Permissions-Policy. Cookie audit found 10 cookies marked insecure, including long-lived SameSite=None analytics/consent cookies.
findings.suggestedFix: Deploy a tested CSP and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure and use the narrowest viable SameSite and lifetime.

findings.summary: Advertising and tracking dominate network activity
findings.evidence: Trackers audit observed 41 third-party origins and 7 known tracker domains. HAR attributed 190/205 requests and 4,988,164/5,018,815 bytes to third-party origins.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce vendors and duplicate analytics, gate non-essential third parties on consent, batch analytics, and load ad/video systems only when they provide immediate value.

findings.summary: A substantial share of current content is unavailable without JavaScript
findings.evidence: Discoverability comparison found only 62% of rendered content words in raw server HTML, so a substantial portion of current content depends on JavaScript.
findings.suggestedFix: Server-render current headline/article lists and ensure core navigation/content remains complete before JavaScript enhancement.

findings.summary: Direction-sensitive CSS is not translation robust
findings.evidence: HTML correctly declares lang=te, but rendered stylesheet evidence contains extensive physical direction rules (81 left, 30 right, 44 margin-left, 24 margin-right) and no demonstrated RTL/logical-property adaptation.
findings.suggestedFix: Replace physical left/right margin, padding, inset, and alignment rules with logical inline/block properties and verify an RTL fixture.

findings.summary: Baseline heap footprint is disproportionately large
findings.evidence: A single homepage state retained about 58 MB self-size across 1,068,632 heap nodes, a high baseline footprint for a news document even though repeated scrolling did not grow it.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce initial DOM/module populations, virtualize or defer offscreen modules, and conditionally initialize advertising and video components.
